title: Poetry Movements and Traditions
text: Poetry is one of the oldest literary forms, with oral traditions predating writing. Ancient traditions include Homeric epic poetry, Sanskrit kavya, and Chinese shi poetry. The sonnet, originating in 13th-century Italy, was perfected by Petrarch and later Shakespeare. English Romantic poets (Wordsworth, Keats, Shelley, Byron) emphasized emotion and nature. The 19th century American poet Walt Whitman pioneered free verse in Leaves of Grass (1855). Emily Dickinson wrote innovative compressed poetry that was largely unpublished in her lifetime. Modernist poetry fragmented traditional forms (Eliot's The Waste Land). Later movements include the Beat Generation (Allen Ginsberg's Howl), confessional poetry, and spoken word/slam poetry.
